title: ST 2110-40: refactoring and improvements
description:
This patch series makes five interrelated changes:

* Expand the ST2110-40 regression test suite to be more thorough
* Refactor the ST2110-40 handoff to st291 to preserve the entire 10-bit array (this is useful for a soon-to-be-submitted patches for ST2038 support so it can leverage common code)
* GUI change to support render the 10-bit array as 10-bit words or 16-bit words, rather than 8-bit bytes
* Extend the ST291 dissector to use the new 10-bit rendering
* Extend the existing RTP dissector to use the new 16-bit rendering for audio samples

Assisted-by: Codex

notes.body:
Hi Devin,

Thanks for your contribution.

May be split your change on multiple MR because there is some change on doc, Qt and dissector.

Hello @alagoutte 

I can certain split the 2110-40 from the GUI changes, but I would have assumed that maintainers wouldn't want to see a gui change proposed without use cases demonstrating it (which is what the RTP and later 291 patch does).

The doc changes go along with the GUI changes, and not sure it makes sense to put those into a third MR.

Of course I'm happy to resubmit in whatever form makes it easiest to review and gets the work merged.

commits_data.title: RTP: Display L16 payloads as 16-bit words
commits_data.message:
RTP: Display L16 payloads as 16-bit words

Recognize static and dynamically signaled L16 payloads and expose their network-order samples as a scoped 16-bit Packet Bytes data source. Retain ordinary byte interpretations and leave non-L16 RTP payloads unchanged.

Add a compressed pcap regression fixture covering stereo and mono L16 payload types plus a non-L16 control packet.

Assisted-by: Codex

commits_data.title: ST 291: Render normalized 10-bit UDW payloads
commits_data.message:
ST 291: Render normalized 10-bit UDW payloads

Have the shared ST 291 layer expose each normalized UDW bitstream with its natural 10-bit interpretation and retain the byte-oriented payload source used by VANC subdissectors.

Scope both representations, together with sources created by native or Lua payload dissectors, to the selected User Data Words item. The enclosing ST 2110-40 ANC packet remains in its original packet context.

Assisted-by: Codex

commits_data.title: Qt: Render and copy 10/16-bit data and scope payload tabs
commits_data.message:
Qt: Render and copy 10/16-bit data and scope payload tabs

Let dissectors describe a data source's natural word width, bit offset, count, byte order, and owning protocol field. Render byte, packed 10-bit, and 16-bit interpretations in Packet Bytes, allow manual interpretation changes, and keep derived tabs scoped to the selected payload.

Make numeric clipboard formats follow the active interpretation while raw text, Base64, MIME, and Hex + ASCII formats retain the source bytes. Document the new display and copy behavior in the User's Guide and release notes.

Assisted-by: Codex

commits_data.title: ST 2110-40: Preserve all ten UDW bits for VANC subdissectors
commits_data.message:
ST 2110-40: Preserve all ten UDW bits for VANC subdissectors

Introduce a transport-independent ST 291 packet representation and normalize DID-through-checksum words in the shared layer. Contiguous transports such as ST 2110-40 and ST 2038 can provide their original packed TVB, while channel-aware transports such as raw SDI can provide logical words after handling raster interleaving and stride.

Centralize parity and checksum processing, canonical 10-bit and byte-oriented UDW construction, and DID/SDID application dispatch. Keep the public subdissector TVB byte-oriented while exposing the full-width TVB through the C context.

Assisted-by: Codex

commits_data.title: ST 2110-40: Expand dissector regression coverage
commits_data.message:
ST 2110-40: Expand dissector regression coverage

Cover decode-as behavior, every registered header field, UDW payloads, empty and malformed packets, checksum and parity handling, and all expert diagnostics. Use a compressed pcap fixture consistent with the other dissector captures.

Assisted-by: Codex
